title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Solicitation Assembly - Terms & Conditions
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which part of the solicitation document contains clauses that are applied uniformly to virtually all procurement actions within the agency, regardless of the specific commodity?
questions.explain: Standard (or General) Terms and Conditions contain boilerplate legal and administrative clauses (e.g., governing law, non-discrimination) applicable to all agency contracts. Special T&Cs are tailored to a specific bid.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency realizes halfway through a multi-year software contract that it is migrating entirely to a new, broader ERP system and no longer needs the software. Which clause gives the agency the right to end the contract without the vendor being at fault?
questions.explain: A Termination for Convenience clause permits the public entity to unilaterally terminate a contract when it is in the best interest of the government to do so, even if the vendor has not breached the contract.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which clause is invoked to protect a contracting party from liability when an unforeseeable, unavoidable event (like a hurricane or pandemic) makes fulfilling the contract impossible?
questions.explain: Force Majeure (or 'Act of God') is a clause that excuses a party from fulfilling their contractual obligations when an extraordinary event or circumstance beyond their control occurs.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: To protect the agency from third-party lawsuits arising due to the negligence of a contractor while performing services, the buyer must ensure the solicitation contains an appropriate:
questions.explain: An Indemnification (or hold harmless) clause requires the contractor to compensate the public agency for harm or loss, and to defend the agency against third-party claims arising from the contractor's actions.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A construction contract states that for every day the project is delayed beyond the final deadline, the contractor will be deducted $1,000 to cover the agency's estimated actual financial losses. This is known as:
questions.explain: Liquidated damages are pre-agreed amounts representing reasonable estimates of actual damages the agency will suffer due to delays. Unlike penalties, which are typically unenforceable in public contracts, liquidated damages strictly represent compensation for actual anticipated harm.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: To allow other governmental entities to use the resulting contract pricing and terms, the buyer should include which type of clause in the solicitation?
questions.explain: A Cooperative Procurement or 'Piggyback' clause allows other public agencies to purchase off the competitively bid contract under the same terms and conditions, leveraging the administrative work of the lead agency.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: If there is a conflict between the Standard Terms & Conditions and the Special Terms & Conditions within a solicitation document, which provision typically dictates how to resolve the conflict?
questions.explain: An Order of Precedence clause explicitly states which section of the contract document governs in the event of a conflict or ambiguity. Usually, Special Terms overrule Standard Terms.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Under what circumstance would a 'Termination for Default' or 'Termination for Cause' clause be appropriately utilized by a public agency?
options: The agency simply decides it wants to use a different vendor
The vendor fails to deliver the goods within the agreed-upon timeline or fails to meet material contract specifications
A natural disaster destroys the vendor's primary manufacturing plant
The agency's budget for the current year has been unexpectedly slashed
questions.explain: Termination for Default/Cause is used when the contractor commits a material breach of the contract, such as failure to deliver, failing to perform required services, or supplying non-conforming goods.
